I'll think through this like the farmer and then lay out the plan.

**My thinking:**

I have 16.9 mu total. My main setup is wheat-maize double cropping — that's what everyone around here does, and it's what I've done for many years. I'll keep about 3 mu for cotton on the sandier piece near the road where wheat doesn't do as well, and put the other 13.9 mu in wheat-maize rotation. So that means 13.9 mu of wheat in winter, then 13.9 mu of maize after wheat harvest, plus 3 mu of cotton for the whole season.

**Wheat** — I plant in early October after the maize comes off. Last year I got about 450 kg/mu, neighbor Old Wang got 500 because he used that new variety "Jimai 22," so I'll try it too — improved seed, costs a bit more but worth it. I put about one bag of compound fertilizer (50 kg of 15-15-15) as base and top-dress with urea at returning-green, maybe 20 kg urea per mu. That comes to around 14 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K per mu. Wheat here needs water — I irrigate before winter, at returning-green, at jointing, and at grain-filling. Four times. I spray twice usually — once for weeds in spring, once for aphids and powdery mildew at heading. Ground is tilled with rotary machine — I pay for the machine service, easier than ploughing.

**Maize** — Direct seed into the wheat stubble, no tillage, the neighbors all do this now and it works fine, saves fuel and time. I use a hybrid seed, "Zhengdan 958" or similar, everyone uses hybrid for maize now — 600 kg/mu is realistic. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea at big trumpet stage. About 18 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. Summer maize mostly gets rain, but I irrigate once or twice if July is dry. One or two sprays for fall armyworm and borer.

**Cotton** — 3 mu. Bt hybrid seed, must be Bt or bollworm destroys you. Cotton is greedy — I give it plenty. About 15 kg N, 8 kg P, 10 kg K per mu, split between base and flowering. I plough before planting to make good beds. Irrigate twice — once before flowering, once at boll-setting. Cotton still needs a lot of spraying even with Bt, at least 4 times for aphids, mites, and whitefly. I expect maybe 250 kg seed cotton per mu — cotton prices aren't great but I've grown it forever and that piece of land suits it.

Family helps at peak times, and I hire a machine for harvest. My costs are real, but skimping on fertilizer means lower yield — I'd rather spend a bit extra than see a thin crop.
